answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a nontransferable stake before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. If voting power is capped per verified credential and new credentials must age before they count, creating a swarm of hollow accounts no longer multiplies influence. A juniper node can publish signed audit evidence to a beacon, letting other participants verify the penalty. The attacker must fund each identity, wait, and risk losing its stake, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than free.
